rewritten_query:
WITH frequent_ss_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ss.ss_item_sk AS item_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 12 AND 31
      AND i.i_category IN ('Children', 'Home', 'Women')
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk, ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 4
),
max_store_sales AS (
    SELECT MAX(csales) AS tpcds_cmax
    FROM (
        SELECT ss.ss_customer_sk AS c_customer_sk,
               SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) AS csales
        FROM store_sales ss
        JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
        JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year = 2001
          AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
        GROUP BY ss.ss_customer_sk
    ) tmp1
),
candidate_sales AS (
    SELECT cs.cs_bill_customer_sk AS customer_sk,
           cs.cs_quantity * cs.cs_list_price AS sales
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND d.d_moy = 7
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM frequent_ss_items f WHERE f.item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT ws.ws_bill_customer_sk AS customer_sk,
           ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price AS sales
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND d.d_moy = 7
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM frequent_ss_items f WHERE f.item_sk = ws.ws_item_sk)
),
candidate_customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_sk
    FROM candidate_sales
    WHERE customer_sk IS NOT NULL
),
qualified_customers AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_customer_sk AS c_customer_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    JOIN candidate_customers cc ON cc.customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
    WHERE c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1940 AND 1946
    GROUP BY ss.ss_customer_sk
    HAVING SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) > 0.95 * (SELECT tpcds_cmax FROM max_store_sales)
)
SELECT SUM(cs.sales)
FROM candidate_sales cs
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM qualified_customers qc
    WHERE qc.c_customer_sk = cs.customer_sk
)
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Push the best_ss_customer aggregation to only candidate bill_customers that actually appear in the filtered catalog/web sales (candidate_sales), instead of aggregating store_sales for all 1940-1946 birth-year customers. Explain shows only ~85 catalog and ~20 web qualifying rows, so the expensive 28M-row aggregation is reduced to a handful of customer lookups.

Simplify frequent_ss_items: remove the unused substring(i_item_desc,1,30) (functionally dependent on i_item_sk PK) and group by ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk (equivalent to d_date since d_date_sk is unique per date). Return DISTINCT item_sk so the CTE is deduplicated once instead of via repeated HashAggregate in each outer branch.

Replace IN (SELECT ...) with EXISTS semi-joins; since both CTEs now return unique keys, EXISTS gives identical semantics with cleaner semi-join plans and NULL handling equivalent to the original IN filters.
Convert comma joins to explicit ANSI JOIN syntax with aliases; keep materialized CTEs (frequent_ss_items, candidate_sales used twice) to avoid recomputation; constant 95/100.0 folded to 0.95.

The join of store_sales to customer in max_store_sales is only used to validate the customer key; if FK integrity is guaranteed it could be dropped (group by ss_customer_sk). Kept here for strict equivalence. An index on store_sales(ss_customer_sk) (ideally including ss_quantity, ss_sales_price) would let qualified_customers use cheap nested-loop lookups for the small candidate customer set.
